root_cause.text: In smb2_unlink(), when SMB2_open_init() or SMB2_close_init() fails, the iov arrays (open_iov, close_iov) are used in rqst without initialization, causing cleanup functions (SMB2_open_free, SMB2_close_free) and smb2_set_related() to operate on uninitialized data, leading to an oops.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `memset(open_iov, 0, sizeof(open_iov))` and `memset(&close_iov, 0, sizeof(close_iov))` before assigning them to rqst[]. It also moves `smb2_set_related()` after the error check for `SMB2_close_init` to avoid calling it on an uninitialized close_iov when the init fails. The CVE description states: "the iovs set @rqst will be left uninitialised, hence calling SMB2_open_free(), SMB2_close_free() or smb2_set_related() on them will oops."

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement assigns the uninitialized open_iov array to rqst[0].rq_iov. If SMB2_open_init() fails, the cleanup function SMB2_open_free() operates on this uninitialized iov, leading to use of garbage pointers and a potential oops.

This statement assigns the address of the uninitialized close_iov array to rqst[1].rq_iov. If SMB2_close_init() fails, the cleanup function SMB2_close_free() and the subsequent smb2_set_related() operate on this uninitialized iov, causing use of uninitialized memory.

This statement calls smb2_set_related() on rqst[1] before checking the return code of SMB2_close_init(). If that initialization failed, the rqst[1].rq_iov points to uninitialized close_iov, and smb2_set_related() accesses uninitialized iov entries, exacerbating the vulnerability and potentially causing an oops.
